meta.prompt: ALS building blocks in compositional hierarchy with AWB mental model mapping

title: ALS Primitives Reference
subtitle: What you can build and how the pieces fit together

layers.label: System
layers.what_it_is: The top-level container — one per project, declared in .als/system.ts.
what_you_can_do: Declare a system_id that namespaces all modules
Register one or more modules
Point to the ALS compiler via authoring.ts
key_constraints: One system per project (.als/ directory)
authoring.ts must use absolute path to installed compiler in standalone projects
system_id is used as the namespace for all downstream skill and delamain IDs
layers.awb_equivalent: The AWB project/workspace — the root container that holds all workflows

layers.label: Module
layers.what_it_is: A versioned bundle of one entity + one or more Delamains + skills, declared in module.ts.
what_you_can_do: Define the entity type that the module operates on
Register Delamains (state machines) for that entity
Register skills (operator-facing Claude Code commands)
Version the whole bundle (v1, v2, etc.) for controlled migration
key_constraints: A module has exactly one primary entity (though the entity can have multiple Delamain fields)
Module path is the mount directory where entity records (markdown files) live
Version is immutable — changes require a new version bundle
layers.awb_equivalent: An AWB workflow group or pipeline family — a cohesive set of workflows around one data concept

layers.label: Entity
layers.what_it_is: The data record — a markdown file with YAML frontmatter that the Delamain state machine operates on.
what_you_can_do: Define typed fields (id, string, date, delamain)
Define the document body with named sections (INPUTS, ANALYSIS, HOOKS, etc.)
Store all workflow state and generated content in one readable file
Use delamain-typed fields to attach state machines to the record
key_constraints: Title source fields must be allow_null: false
A delamain-typed field is the ONLY way to trigger a Delamain on this entity
One delamain-typed field = one active state machine on the record
Two delamain-typed fields = two independent parallel state machines
session-field values (from resumable states) are implicitly added to frontmatter at runtime
layers.awb_equivalent: The AWB work item / job record — the thing flowing through the pipeline

layers.label: Delamain
layers.what_it_is: A state machine that operates on an entity, triggered by a delamain-typed field — the core runtime concept in ALS.
what_you_can_do: Define phases (logical groupings of states)
Define states — each owned by either an agent or an operator
Define transitions between states (advance, rework, exit)
Mark states as resumable for crash recovery
Declare agent bindings (provider, path to agent .md file)
key_constraints: No sub-Delamains — Delamains cannot call each other
A Delamain is triggered by a delamain-typed field on an entity — not by another Delamain
Two Delamains on the same entity require two separate delamain-typed fields
Must declare provider (anthropic or openai) on every agent state
Resumable states must declare session-field
layers.awb_equivalent: An AWB pipeline/workflow — but commit-driven (not CLI-triggered) and always attached to a specific entity field

layers.label: State
layers.what_it_is: A single node in the Delamain state machine — owned by either an agent (auto-runs) or an operator (human gate).
what_you_can_do: Make a state agent-owned: it runs automatically when the dispatcher finds the entity in that state
Make a state operator-owned: it waits for a human decision via the pipeline skill
Make a state terminal: workflow ends here (completed, cancelled)
Mark a state resumable: dispatcher can recover a crashed agent session
Mark a state initial: starting state for new entity records
key_constraints: Agent states must declare provider
Agent states must declare path to the agent .md file
Resumable agent states must declare session-field
Only one initial state per Delamain
Terminal states have no outgoing transitions
layers.awb_equivalent: An AWB step/node — but split cleanly into human (operator) and machine (agent) types with no ambiguity

layers.label: Transition
layers.what_it_is: A declared edge between states — classes: advance (forward progress), rework (go back), exit (cancel or complete).
what_you_can_do: advance: move from one state to the next in the happy path
rework: send the entity back to a previous state for another pass
exit: move directly to a terminal state (cancel from anywhere, or complete at end)
Declare multi-from transitions: same transition class from multiple source states to one target
key_constraints: Transitions must reference states that exist in the same Delamain
The dispatcher commits the transition — not the operator directly
The agent selects the outgoing transition from the legal options in runtime-manifest
layers.awb_equivalent: AWB step connections/edges — but explicitly typed (advance/rework/exit) rather than generic arrows

layers.label: Agent
layers.what_it_is: A Claude (or OpenAI) model invocation bound to a state — given the entity record and a markdown instruction file, it does work and chooses the next transition.
what_you_can_do: Read and write the entity record (YAML frontmatter + markdown sections)
Call external tools and APIs (e.g. FliHub for transcript fetch)
Run parallel sub-agents for tasks like analysis
Choose from the legal outgoing transitions declared in runtime-manifest
Resume from a stored session ID if the dispatcher crashed mid-run
key_constraints: Agent receives the entity record + agent .md instructions as context
Agent must select a valid outgoing transition — it cannot create new ones
Agent output is committed to git by the dispatcher, then merged to integration
Agent runs in an isolated git worktree per dispatch
layers.awb_equivalent: An AWB agent step — but with formal state-machine bindings and git-commit-driven lifecycle

layers.label: Operator
layers.what_it_is: A human gate — the dispatcher pauses at operator-owned states and waits for a human to act via the pipeline skill.
what_you_can_do: Review agent-generated content in the entity record
Make selections, provide input, or edit sections
Advance to the next state (progress)
Rework back to a previous state (reject/refine)
Exit to cancelled (abort)
key_constraints: Operator states require no path or provider declaration
The pipeline skill is the interface — operators don't edit entity files directly in normal flow
The dispatcher will not advance an operator-owned state automatically
layers.awb_equivalent: An AWB human-in-the-loop approval step — but with formal transition choices (advance/rework/exit) rather than free-form approval

layers.label: Skill
layers.what_it_is: A Claude Code slash command — a markdown instruction file deployed to .claude/skills/ and invokable as /skill-id.
what_you_can_do: Create operator-facing commands (e.g. /fli-launch-pipeline, /fli-launch-manage)
Surface entity records needing attention at operator gates
Provide CRUD for entity records (create, list, inspect, cancel)
Run ALS system operations (deploy, validate, bootup, etc.)
File issues to external systems (e.g. /als:ghost-line)
key_constraints: Skills are markdown files — Claude reads and follows them as instructions
Skills are deployed from .als/modules/<id>/v1/skills/ to .claude/skills/ via alsc deploy
Skills are not visible in the current Claude Desktop session after deploy — requires session restart
Skills do not replace the dispatcher — they handle operator-owned states only
layers.awb_equivalent: AWB operator console / UI commands — but implemented as Claude Code slash commands rather than a web interface

layers.label: Dispatcher
layers.what_it_is: A background Bun process that watches git HEAD for entity files in agent-owned states and invokes agents automatically.
what_you_can_do: Poll git HEAD every 30 seconds for agent-owned state changes
Create isolated git worktrees per dispatch
Invoke agents via Claude Agent SDK
Auto-commit agent output and chosen transition
Merge worktrees back to integration checkout
Resume crashed agent sessions using stored session-field values
key_constraints: Dispatcher requires deployed .claude/delamains/<name>/ — alsc deploy must run first
Dispatcher requires bun install in dispatcher/ directory before first run
Dispatcher dies when the Claude Code session ends — re-run /als:bootup each session
Dispatcher only reads committed git HEAD — uncommitted changes are invisible to it
No skill exists to deploy (filed: nfrith/als#2) — deploy must be run manually
layers.awb_equivalent: The AWB execution engine / task runner — but commit-driven and file-system based rather than API/event driven
